title: Indian-Origin NASA Astronaut Anil Menon Reaches ISS on Historic First Mission

body:
Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon has arrived at the International Space Station, marking the beginning of his first-ever spaceflight — an eight-month mission that will see him conduct groundbreaking experiments in medicine, semiconductor manufacturing, and AI-assisted healthcare.

A Historic Launch

Menon launched on July 14 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan aboard the Roscosmos Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft, alongside Russian cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina. He will serve as part of Expeditions 74 and 75, with a planned return to Earth in spring 2027.

Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, to an Indian father from Kerala and a Ukrainian mother, Menon is an emergency medicine physician, mechanical engineer, and colonel in the United States Space Force. He was selected as part of NASA's 2021 astronaut class.

Turning Station Water Into IV Fluid

Among the most consequential experiments Menon will conduct is testing a system that can produce intravenous (IV) fluids directly from the station's potable water supply. Known as IVGEN Mini, the technology could prove essential for future deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars, where medical supplies cannot be easily replenished.

The system filters station drinking water to remove particulates and mineral ions, then combines the processed water with premeasured sodium chloride to create sterile, medical-grade IV fluid on demand. Current IV fluid has a shelf life of only 16 months, far too short for three-year deep-space missions.

Semiconductor Crystals and AI-Powered Medicine

Menon will also advance research on manufacturing semiconductor crystals in microgravity, with the goal of producing higher-quality components for high-performance computing, AI, and advanced medical devices. Additionally, he will perform ultrasound studies using augmented reality and AI technologies, developing capabilities that could reduce or eliminate the need for Earth-based medical guidance during future missions.

A Family of Space Explorers

His wife, Anna Menon, is also an astronaut who flew into space in September 2024 as part of SpaceX's Polaris Dawn mission. Anil Menon previously served as the medical director at SpaceX and as a flight surgeon supporting NASA's ISS crew. His great-grandfather is Chettur Sankaran Nair, a prominent figure in India's independence movement — a remarkable family legacy that now spans continents and the stars.
